turns.t: Hello, doctor. I've been told to come back since the operation, because my stomach's been playing up. I'm trying to remember what I wanted to ask.
It was your gallbladder operation, wasn't it, a month ago? ~
That's the one. Oh, it'll come to me. The hiccups, yes! I get hiccups, and belching, after I eat. Not every time.
Do the hiccups go on for long?
10 minutes, 15 minutes. And then I belch, loudly. It's very embarrassing at the golf club.
Any vomiting?
No. No vomiting.
Let me go through your tablets with you.

Right, I've got a list. Omeprazole, 20 mg, once a day. Ramipril, 5 mg once a day. Paracetamol, 500 mg when I need it. And, hold on, the other one, for the nerves, I think it's amitriptyline, maybe 10 mg, at night?
So the amitriptyline, 10 mg, at night, as you recall it. I'll check the record. Any other medical history?
High blood pressure, and an irritable bowel.
Let me examine your tummy. ~
Go on.
The scars from the keyhole operation are healing nicely, and your tummy is soft and not tender.
That's a relief. ~

Hiccups and belching after a meal, in someone who's had abdominal surgery, are usually due to swallowing air, eating too fast, or acid reflux. I'd say this is most likely excess air-swallowing and reflux after the operation.
Will it pass? ~
Usually it does, within a few months. I'd like to arrange a blood test, to make sure everything's in order after the operation, including your liver.
Fine. Could any of my tablets be doing it? ~
I don't think so, but I'll look at them again when I see you next. ~
Do I keep taking them all in the meantime? ~
Yes, don't change anything yet. ~
And golf? ~
Golf is fine, just don't eat a big meal right before you play. ~
Eat slowly, take smaller meals, avoid fizzy drinks and chewing gum, and sit upright for an hour after eating.
I like a fizzy drink. ~
Switch to water for a few weeks and see. ~
Right. ~
I'd like to see you again in four weeks, to see how the belching is.
Four weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~
